column1: # The names of the zone that stay Dutch (card rename-public-api, 2026-10-18). Until then the list held every name that
# code outside this repository read; the distribution regelspraak-toolchain now follows the renames, so what remains is
# what must keep its spelling for a reason outside that code:
#   toka: the toka/ zone is not renamed, and its two tests read these names (rename.py freeze over a copy of
#         toka/src/test/java; file: the test that reads the name most; count: its reads of the zone in both tests);
#   spelling: the zone fixes the spelling itself (see below);
#   grammar: a parser rule or label of the RegelSpraak grammar, or the Context class ANTLR makes of it: the rules follow
#         the Dutch RegelSpraak specification and stay Dutch (CLAUDE.md, Conventions; owner's decision 2026-10-18);
#   visible: the distribution writes the spelling of the constant into its HTTP API, its OpenAPI document, its CLI
#         output or its explanation prose (name(), values() or a printed enum), where nothing outside the code may change.
# file: the file that reads the name most; count: its reads.
# The zone writes the spelling of some constants into messages (ResolvedRegel.Soort: RuleChecker prints soort.name().toLowerCase()
# in its diagnostics) and its tests pass them as strings (IrPath.regel(..., "BEREKENING", ...)); a message changes with no card but meldingscodes.
# The v0 values of spec/proposals/v1-naamtabel.json (section waarden) are the names of the frontend's enum constants, and SpellingTest
# reads them from name(); spec/proposals/ keeps v0 names as they are (CLAUDE.md, Conventions), so these constants keep theirs.
